title: ChatChunk
$comment: Role: the one canonical streaming event (docs/architecture.md §3.1; ocai/chat/types/stream.py ChatChunk) in omit-absent wire form — the shape `chat.chunk` payload every provider frame becomes and the unit StreamAccumulator.fold consumes. `type` says which optional lanes are populated; everything else is absent. The `type` code is an OPEN string vocabulary: an unknown wire kind is LEGAL and preserved verbatim (total decode, never a raise). The typed delta union lives in deltas.schema.json; the terminal record lives in stream_end.schema.json.
description: One canonical streaming event: the open event kind, the stream/part coordinates, and exactly the lanes that kind populates (part skeleton or final, typed delta, usage update, finish record, wire-shaped error, or the authoritative terminal StreamEnd).

type.description: The open event kind. Known canonical values: streamStart, streamStop (terminal; carries `end`), partStart (carries the `part` skeleton), partDelta (carries `delta`), partStop (may carry the authoritative final `part`, which MUST equal the delta accumulation — the fold law), usage, finish, metadata, error, raw, ping. Unknown wire kinds are LEGAL and preserved verbatim.

seq.description: The chunk's zero-based position in the canonical stream, stamped by the emitting codec — the replay/fold ordering key.

index.description: The content-part slot this event concerns, for the partStart/partDelta/partStop kinds. Streams may omit it; the accumulator then targets the most recently started slot.

part.description: The part skeleton (partStart) or the authoritative final part (partStop).

delta.description: The incremental update (partDelta), applied to the open slot with append semantics per delta type.

usage.description: A consumption update (usage). Mid-stream updates are provisional; the terminal StreamEnd's usage overrides them in the fold.

usage_cumulative.description: Whether `usage` replaces (true) or extends (false) previous updates; absent when the wire does not say.

finish.description: The stop record (finish). Mid-stream records are provisional; the terminal StreamEnd's finish overrides them in the fold.

error.description: The wire-shaped mid-stream error (error) — data, not just an exception, so a recorded stream replays identically to a live one.

end.description: The authoritative terminal record (streamStop): final usage/finish and the stream's FidelityReport. A stream that ends without one was aborted, and the accumulator seals its open parts with extensions["ocai.incomplete"].

raw_event.description: The untouched provider frame this chunk was decoded from, for power users and the wiretap archive. Verbatim, deliberately unconstrained, and excluded from semantic equality (spec/canonical-json.md §8).

errorInfo.$comment: ocai/chat/types/stream.py ErrorInfo — a mid-stream error in wire shape. A plain value object (no IR envelope), like span.
errorInfo.description: A mid-stream error as data: the canonical taxonomy code, the provider's verbatim payload, and retryability when known.

code.description: The open canonical error-taxonomy code. Known canonical values: rate_limit, auth, context_length, content_filter, transient, unknown. Unknown values are legal and preserved verbatim.

native.description: The provider's verbatim error payload, unconstrained.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the call could succeed, when the taxonomy mapping knows.
